uncited: It builds on [Real-time shell space rendering](11590-real-time-shell-space-rendering.md) by applying specific texture sampling strategies to the shell space to simulate volumetric microgeometry (such as fur) rather than just solid volume.
Perturb the vertices of the base model along their surface normals by an offset amount $d_i$.
Render the perturbed model into a framebuffer.
Sample the shell volume texture at the corresponding radial level for each fragment.
A variant specifically for rendering fur by generating concentric shells around a model.
Each shell is rendered with an alpha-blended texture sampled from the fur volume at the corresponding level.
It allows for real-time rendering of microgeometry with global lighting effects.

*   **Remedy:** Add small textures rendered normal to the surface across all edges, faded in as the edge approaches the silhouette [S1, unofficial]. *Note: Some implementations omit this step (fins) for simplicity, accepting the gap artifact [S1, unofficial].*

The claim states that the remedy involves adding small textures rendered normal to the surface, faded in as the edge approaches the silhouette. Source [S1] confirms that the original Lengyel method uses 'fins' (quads perpendicular to the model) to remedy gaps. However, the source explicitly states that the specific implementation discussed in the text ('our implementation') does *not* use fins ('For this reason, we have not yet added fins into our model'). The claim attributes the 'fins' approach as the standard remedy but notes that 'some implementations omit this step'. While the description of the remedy (fins/normal textures) matches the Lengyel method described in the text, the text clarifies that the specific implementation being analyzed omits it. The claim is partially supported because it correctly describes the remedy mentioned in the literature (Lengyel's fins) but incorrectly implies it is the general solution used in the context of the provided text's implementation, which explicitly omits it. More critically, the claim says 'Add small textures rendered normal to the surface... [S1, unofficial]'. The text says Lengyel adds 'fins' (quads). The claim's description of 'small textures rendered normal' is a slightly different phrasing of 'fins'. The text says 'Lengyel adds fins... These shells are also sampled into the fur volume'. The claim is supported regarding the existence of the remedy in the literature cited by S1, but the 'unofficial' tag and the specific implementation details make it partial because the text's primary subject omits it.
